title: An eight-vertex counterexample to the Li–Weng rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture (Conjecture 6.12 of arXiv:2004.06285v2)
exact_endpoint: Rainbow.mathdb_346167_literal : ¬∀ (n : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), 8 ≤ n → H.Connected → Hᶜ.Connected → n ≤ Rainbow.sourceRvd H + Rainbow.sourceRvd Hᶜ, with sourceRvd the literal least number of colours of a rainbow vertex-disconnection colouring (source 'S + x or S + y rainbow' clause for adjacent pairs)
scope: Li and Weng, Further results on the rainbow vertex-disconnection of graphs, arXiv:2004.06285v2 Conjecture 6.12 (5.12 in v1; Bull. Malays. Math. Sci. Soc. 44 (2021)): rvd(G) + rvd(Ḡ) ≥ n for connected G, Ḡ of order n ≥ 8. False: an explicit connected 8-vertex graph G (masks 202,225,232,149,232,22,23,31) with connected complement has rvd(G) = 4 and rvd(Ḡ) = 3, sum 7. Supporting evidence: 74 of the 9,888 eligible order-8 isomorphism classes fail, and three connected one-vertex extensions fail at order 9 (sum 8 < 9), so the threshold is not merely off by one.

substantive_reason: It refutes a published Nordhaus–Gaddum-type lower-bound conjecture for the rainbow vertex-disconnection number at its stated threshold, with exact values rvd = 4 and 3 proved by short arguments and complete cut certificates. The order-9 failures show the conjectured bound fails beyond the threshold, not just at n = 8. Significance is modest: a small, easily found finite refutation with no replacement general bound.
